audit.whatIsWrong: content 'early' and 'wants.foe[0]' label Vision of Empire as (E) and Nevermove as (W) — swapped from enemyKit, which has W=Vision of Empire (long-range poke/reveal, range 5500-7500) and E=Nevermove (the root, range 850). 'wants.foe[0]' also calls Vision of Empire a root, which it is not.
audit.why: enemyKit is the authority on slot letters; Swain's real kit is P Ravenous Flock, Q Death's Hand, W Vision of Empire, E Nevermove, R Demonic Ascension. Only Nevermove roots — Vision of Empire deals damage/slow/reveal at long range.
audit.corrected: Swapped the (E)/(W) letters in 'early' and 'wants.foe[0]' to match enemyKit, and stopped calling Vision of Empire a root.

audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[0-5].side all read Skill (rating 5-6/10) while content win[0-5] all read Swain, and content's whys/spikes/early/mid give detailed, kit-grounded reasons Swain wins levels 1 through first item (Nevermove root + Ravenous Flock sustain, Demonic Ascension at 6, drain-tank item scaling).
audit.why: phases[N].side and win[N] are the same row and must agree. packet.defects flags exactly this (winrate 53.98% for Bard but chart gave Swain 6/7 stages vs 0 — actually the true fix is the full-layer side was never updated to match the correct, well-argued content side).
audit.corrected: Moved phases[0-5].side to Swain (phases[6] already agrees at Skill) with matching rating bumps and grounded whys taken from the same reasoning as content.

audit.why: Spikes correctly flag level 2 (Nevermove+Vision of Empire root-combo threat), level 6 (Demonic Ascension wins extended trades), first item (drain-tank snowball), late (levels out to CC-first skill check).

edits.before: Swain wins the opening: his E (Vision of Empire) and W (Nevermove) give him long-range roots that outrange your comfortable trade patterns, and his passive heals him off any minion or champ he damages so the poke war swings his way. Never line up with your ADC where his E can root you both, and use his mana-hungry early game to trade only when his roots are down. Bank Magical Journey to break the root chain.
edits.after: Swain wins the opening: his W (Vision of Empire) pokes at long range while his E (Nevermove) roots, and his passive heals him off any minion or champ he damages, so the poke war swings his way. Never line up with your ADC where his E can root you both, and use his mana-hungry early game to trade only when his root is down. Bank Magical Journey to break the root chain.

edits.before: Chain Nevermove (W) and Vision of Empire (E) roots to lock you for a full combo
edits.after: Root you with Nevermove (E), then Vision of Empire (W) poke for the full combo

edits.before: Meep-chip the contacts and collect the first chimes — the wanderer's ledger opens.
edits.after: Nevermove (E) outranges your trades, and Ravenous Flock heals him off every poke landed.

edits.before: Q threats begin: every wall adjacency is a stun audition.
edits.after: Nevermove threatens the full combo — stay off your ADC's line.

edits.before: Full kit: shrine the sustain, tunnel the angles, and Q the geometry.
edits.after: Poke-and-heal grinds you down while his passive sustains the trade.

edits.before: Chime economy: collect on the move and return with meep upgrades — absence is investment.
edits.after: His drain sustain still beats your single-target pick pressure through this whole stretch.

edits.before: Tempered Fate online — the map's biggest moments now have a stasis clause.
edits.after: Demonic Ascension turns every extended trade into one Swain wins outright.

edits.before: First item: the meeps chunk and the portals make your jungler ambidextrous.
edits.after: His first drain-tank item deepens the sustained-exchange advantage his way.

edits.before: Late Bard edits fights: R the engage or the objective, Q the chokes, and tunnel the team to the answer.
edits.after: With full items and both ultimates online, the lane evens into a skill check on who lands hard CC first.

edits.before: Bait the answer, start the chain, and let your carry collect — engage trades are all-or-nothing; pick the all.
edits.after: Drop W (Health shrine) before he pokes — it only heals once shielded, so pre-place it and buy anti-heal early.

edits.before: Engaging into a banked disengage — the chain that starts answered is a donation with intentions.
edits.after: Sitting in his zone while it recharges gifts free Death's Hand poke — reposition until it resets.

edits.before: - Swain Nevermove: matchup-defining — The root that decides — dodge it and the general farms regret. Read it before every duo step-up. - Your E Magical Journey answers exactly one disaster per cooldown. - Spend the R on swing moments only.
edits.after: - Swain Nevermove is 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s — the root that decides, dodge it and the general farms regret. Read it before every duo step-up. - Your E Magical Journey answers exactly one disaster per cooldown. - Spend the R on swing moments only.

notes: Real ability-slot bug found and fixed (like the Nilah/Cassiopeia calibration examples): enemyKit confirms Swain W=Vision of Empire (long-range poke/reveal), E=Nevermove (the root); 'early' and 'wants.foe[0]' had the letters swapped and called Vision of Empire a root, which it is not — fixed both, and left whys[0]/spikes text alone since those don't name letters. Also fixed the level-chart disagreement packet.defects flagged: full phases[0-5].side all read Skill while content win[0-5] read Swain with detailed, kit-grounded support (Nevermove range/root, Ravenous Flock sustain, Demonic Ascension at 6, drain-tank scaling at first item); moved phases[0-5].side to Swain with matching rating/why, leaving phases[6] as Skill since it already agreed with win[6]. dosFull[1]/dontsFull[2] were tradeGood/tradeBad copy-paste bleed, rewritten to match their own titles. breakdown.cooldowns now carries Nevermove's real per-rank cooldown, resolving the 'no cooldown-sequencing advice' defect too.
